$comment: Reasoning-effort capability OVERRIDES — how `/think` reaches a model this build has never
heard of. Copy this file to either layer and edit; both are optional and both start absent:
~/.prometheus/effort-capabilities.json          your machine
<project>/.prometheus/effort-capabilities.json  checked in with a repo
The built-in table (packages/core/src/ai/effort/rules.ts) is always loaded FIRST, then the
user layer, then the project layer. Precedence is append order: the resolver scores how
SPECIFIC each match is and breaks a tie in favour of the LATER rule, so a rule here with the
same match as a builtin wins, and one with a narrower match wins outright. There is no merge
step and no override key — later simply wins.
A rule is { id, match, cap }.
match  — any of: runtime, capability, capabilityAbsent, modelIdPrefix, modelIdRegex,
locality. More fields = more specific. `capability`/`capabilityAbsent` test what a
runtime PROBE reported (Ollama's /api/show `capabilities`) and outrank every
name match, because a model id is a guess and a probe is an answer.
IMPORTANT, and the thing people hit first: order only breaks TIES. A rule that
matches LESS specifically than the one you meant to replace does not win, however
late it is loaded. To override a probe-driven builtin you must match the probe too
— add `capability: "thinking"` (or `capabilityAbsent`) alongside your regex.
Verified: a `{runtime, modelIdRegex}` rule loses to the builtin
`ollama-openai-shim-thinking`; add `capability` and it wins.
cap    — mechanism (see below), `supported` (which of off|low|medium|high|max this pair can
really express), plus the fields that mechanism needs, and a one-sentence `note`
shown to the user whenever the tier is degraded.
Mechanisms, and what each one needs:
effort-enum         field + enumMap     a string in the body (reasoning_effort, …)
token-budget        field + budgetMap   an integer budget; budgetBounds clamps it
native-graded       field + enumMap     a graded field in a non-OpenAI shape
binary-toggle       field               on/off only (onValue/offValue, default true/false)
template-kwarg      kwarg               a Jinja kwarg the runtime forwards
system-prompt-line  promptMap           a literal line the model was TRAINED to read
prompt-soft-switch  promptMap           a trained-on token appended to a turn
always-on                               it reasons, and the depth cannot be moved
none                                    no reasoning control at all
Version-bound your regexes. Reasoning support changes WITHIN a family — Gemma 2/3 cannot
think and Gemma 4 can — so a family-level pattern is wrong within one generation.
A malformed rule is reported at startup and skipped; the rest of the file still loads.
Three worked examples are below. Delete `_examples` and put real entries in
`rules` — `rules` is the only key that is read.
